hints.title: Identify the terms left after subtraction
hints.body: Subtracting the first partial sum from the later one leaves a consecutive block of terms. Identify the surviving term indices, then write the first and last terms of that block and of the first block using the GP term formula.
hints.recap: Subtracting partial sums isolates a consecutive block.
hints.pitfall: The exponent in term n is one less than its index.
hints.pause: Write the two blocks with correct indices and match their corresponding terms.

recall.reminder: Subtracting partial sums isolates a consecutive block.

hints.title: Factor out the shared block multiplier
hints.body: Corresponding terms in equal-length GP blocks differ by one common multiplier. Find it by dividing a later-block term by its matching earlier-block term. All terms are positive, so the first block sum is nonzero.
hints.recap: The exponent difference records how far one block is shifted along the progression.
hints.pitfall: The length of a block and the shift between blocks need not be equal.
hints.pause: Derive the block-sum identity and compare it with the given equation for k.

recall.reminder: A fixed shift in GP term indices multiplies corresponding terms by the same power of the common ratio.

hints.title: Apply the integer restriction
hints.body: Use your block identity to express the requested multiplier in terms of the common ratio. Then apply the stated integer restriction to that ratio.
hints.recap: An increasing positive power is smallest at the least allowed positive input.
hints.pause: Find the least allowed ratio, justify that it minimises your expression and evaluate the multiplier.

recall.reminder: An increasing positive power is smallest at the least allowed positive input.

solution:
Terms 21–30 are r20 times terms 1–10, so S30−S20=r20S10. Since S10>0, comparison with kS10 gives k=r20.

The smallest integer r>1 is 2, yielding k=220.

Answer B.
